questions.questionText: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'reluctant'.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.questionText: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'scarce'.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; abundant is the opposite.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?

options.text: The girls' books were on the desk.
The girls's books were on the desk.
The girl's books were on the desk. (three girls)
The girls books were on the desk.

questions.explanation: The plural possessive girls' indicates books belonging to more than one girl.

questions.questionText: Which word is an adjective in the sentence 'The narrow road was flooded'?
questions.explanation: Narrow describes the noun road.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The boy is breaking the window.
The window was broken by the boy.
The boy will break the window.

questions.explanation: The subject receives the action in the passive construction.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'She studied hard, ___ she passed the examination.'
questions.explanation: So shows the result of studying hard.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?

options.text: Neither the teacher nor the pupils were late.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils be late.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils is late.
Neither the teacher nor the pupils was late.

questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, pupils.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to state or identify something exactly.

questions.questionText: Which register is most appropriate for a formal letter to a school head?
questions.explanation: A formal letter requires respectful, appropriate language.

questions.questionText: Which reading skill involves looking quickly for a specific date or name?
questions.explanation: Scanning is used to locate specific information quickly.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?

options.text: Please sit down the teacher, said.

questions.explanation: A direct quotation is separated from the reporting clause with appropriate punctuation.

questions.questionText: Which word is a synonym for 'diligent'?
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a metaphor?

options.text: The classroom was as hot as a furnace.

questions.explanation: A metaphor directly describes one thing as another.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a report?

options.text: To persuade readers to buy something
To present factual information in an organised way

questions.explanation: Reports present organised information, often based on observations or findings.

questions.questionText: Which opening is most appropriate for a formal complaint letter?

options.text: I am writing to express my concern about...

questions.explanation: The first option uses an appropriate formal register.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct word to complete: "Scarcely had the bell rung ___ the learners entered the hall."
questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction is "Scarcely/Hardly ... when" (whereas "No sooner ... than").

questions.questionText: Select the sentence with correct conditional structure (Third Conditional):

options.text: If she would have studied, she passed.
If she studied harder, she will have passed.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed with a distinction.
Had she studied harder, she would pass yesterday.

questions.explanation: Third conditional uses: If + Past Perfect, ... would have + Past Participle.

questions.questionText: Which word is closest in meaning to "ambiguous"?

options.text: Open to more than one interpretation

questions.explanation: "Ambiguous" describes statements having multiple unclear meanings.

questions.questionText: Change to passive voice: "The committee will announce the results tomorrow."

options.text: The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The results are announced by the committee tomorrow.
Tomorrow announced the results the committee.
The results will have been announce by the committee.

questions.explanation: Future simple passive uses "will be + past participle".

questions.questionText: Choose the correct preposition: "The new prefect is popular ___ all the junior classes."
questions.explanation: Standard collocation: "popular with" people.

questions.questionText: Identify the figure of speech in: "The dry maize leaves whispered secrets in the evening wind."
questions.explanation: Leaves are given the human ability to whisper secrets (personification).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?

options.text: Although it was raining; we walked to school.
He asked me; where I lived.
She bought; apples, oranges, and bananas.
The match was postponed; heavy rain had flooded the pitch.

questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom "to turn over a new leaf":

options.text: To reform one's behaviour and make a fresh start

questions.explanation: "Turn over a new leaf" means to adopt better conduct or start afresh.

questions.questionText: Complete correctly: "Each of the athletes ___ given a certificate after the race."
questions.explanation: "Each" is grammatically singular and takes singular verb "was".

questions.questionText: Which word is correctly spelt?
questions.explanation: Accommodation has double c and double m.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct question tag: "Let's review the past paper before dusk, ___?"
questions.explanation: Suggestions starting with "Let's" take the tag "shall we?".

questions.questionText: Which option best replaces the phrasal verb in: "The school head called off the assembly due to the storm"?
questions.explanation: "Call off" means to cancel a scheduled event ("put off" = postpone).

questions.questionText: Select the most formal closing for a job application letter addressed "Dear Mr. Mupfumi,".
questions.explanation: When addressing a recipient by name (Dear Mr./Ms. X), formal letters close with "Yours sincerely,". ("Yours faithfully," pairs with "Dear Sir/Madam,".)

questions.questionText: Choose the word opposite in meaning (antonym) to "frugal":
questions.explanation: "Frugal" means economical/sparing; the opposite is "extravagant" (wasteful).

questions.questionText: Identify the grammatical function of the underlined clause in: "Although he was exhausted, he finished the marathon."
questions.explanation: "Although he was exhausted" modifies the main verb showing contrast/concession.

questions.questionText: Complete accurately: "I wish I ___ more time to check my essay yesterday."
questions.explanation: Wishes about past regrets take the Past Perfect ("had had").

questions.questionText: Which word is a synonym for "mitigate" as used in "Trees help mitigate soil erosion"?
questions.explanation: "Mitigate" means to reduce the severity or harm of something.

questions.questionText: Spot the sentence free of ambiguity:

options.text: Saw a man with binoculars on the hill.
Using a telescope, the astronomer observed Jupiter clearly.
The dog chased the cat until it was tired.

questions.explanation: Option C has a clear subject ("the astronomer") matching the opening participial phrase.

questions.questionText: Complete: "The learners are looking forward ___ visiting Great Zimbabwe next term."
questions.explanation: "Look forward to" takes a gerund (-ing noun): "looking forward to visiting".

questions.questionText: Choose the correct reported speech for: "Why didn't you attend practice?" the coach asked Tatenda.

options.text: The coach asked Tatenda why he hadn't attended practice.
The coach asked Tatenda why didn't he attend practice.
The coach asked Tatenda that why he hadn't attended practice.
The coach asked Tatenda why hadn't he attend practice.

questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order (subject before verb) and shift past simple to past perfect ("hadn't attended").
